name: security-csp-enforcement-review
intent: Effective Content Security Policy enforcement across headers, HTML policies and frame contexts
artifacts: All response CSP headers, meta policies, script insertion callsite, browser console/violation records and legitimate script bootstrap.
trace: Resolve the policy applying to the protected document and sink. Separate Report-Only from enforcement; combine multiple enforced policies as simultaneous restrictions. Follow nonce creation and propagation into the actual inserted script.
experiment: In an owned fixture, compare the legitimate nonce-bearing bootstrap with one inert untrusted script marker at the same sink and capture whether execution occurs.
disproof: An unsafe-looking directive or report-only violation is not a bypass; CSP absence alone does not establish an injection path.
repair: Retest allowed bootstrap and rejected untrusted insertion under the repaired effective policies and the same browser context.
branch_decisions: If several enforced policies are present, test the intersection, not the most permissive header in isolation. Attribute the tested policy to the actual document/frame. A nonce read by privileged automation is not an attacker-readable nonce; strict-dynamic and parser-inserted versus dynamic scripts need separate consumer evidence.
operational_method: Retain response headers and the position/time of each meta-delivered policy relative to the challenged resource. A meta policy does not retrospectively block earlier content and cannot express every header-delivered directive. Identify unsupported/ignored directives from the actual engine diagnostics. Compare insertion after activation with the same harmless marker before activation; only the applicable enforced policy can serve as the tested security gate.
